entities.title: Keep .dev folders out of the deployed games
entities.summary: The builds skip .dev when they copy public/, and the game workflow fails a build whose dist/ holds a .dev folder.
entities.context: build.mjs copies public/ with cpSync("public", site, { recursive: true }), which copies dot-folders, so public/.dev/folder.json lands at dist/games/retro/hivestorm/.dev/folder.json (checked by running the build). Wrangler's assets upload ignores only .assetsignore, _redirects and _headers unless an .assetsignore says otherwise, and Hivestorm has none, so the deploy would serve the file at icelander.net/games/retro/hivestorm/.dev/folder.json. It holds no secret, only a description of the folder. Rally, Shatterbelt and Samosa copied public/ the same way, and Rally's public/.dev/folder.json was already served.

options.title: Leave it
options.consequences: A small JSON file describing the page folder is public. Nothing else changes.

options.title: Skip .dev when copying public/ (build.mjs)
options.consequences: dist/ holds only the game; a change to build.mjs in each game that copies public/.

options.title: Add an .assetsignore to public/ listing .dev
options.consequences: The file is built but not uploaded; .assetsignore itself is never uploaded.

options.title: Write no .dev folder in public/
options.consequences: The page folder goes undocumented, against AGENTS.md's rule that every maintained folder documents itself.

entities.decision: Skip .dev when copying public/ (build.mjs), and check every game's build for .dev folders in CI.
entities.rationale: .dev files document the code for its maintainers and are not part of the game. The CI check also catches a game that copies a folder some other way.

entities.title: Share code between the web games?
entities.summary: Moving the copied online play, high-score table, page look and name rules into one packages/game-kit/ ends the rule that the games share no code at build time.
entities.context: online.ts is identical in Rally, Hivestorm and Shatterbelt; look.ts differs by two lines across four Workers; Samosa's name rules are copied into three games; the score Workers repeat one capability and one Seed state machine. Two open backlog items in games/rally/src ask for a check that the copies agree. Each game is deployed on its own, and changed-games.sh picks the games to deploy by the files changed.

options.title: Share them in packages/game-kit/
options.consequences: One copy of the code and of its views; a change to the kit deploys every game that uses it, at once.

options.title: Keep the copies and check they agree
options.consequences: Each game stays independent; a CI check catches drift; the explorer keeps showing the shared behaviour once per game.

origin.description: The owner asked for a plan to refactor retro-games so that it shows everything the cyberspace explorer can show, and approved its Phase 0.

entities.title: Split the long main files?
entities.summary: Moving each game's screen machine out of its main file, and Gambit's screens into their own scripts, is the riskiest step of the plan for the least gain in the explorer.
entities.context: Rally's main.ts and Shatterbelt's run the screen machines their Screen and Scene state diagrams draw, alongside the wiring; Shatterbelt keeps render, input and sound in src/ rather than src/ui/; Gambit's main.gd builds every screen. Hivestorm's screens follow the engine's own phase, already drawn as Game, so it needs no split.

options.title: Split them
options.consequences: Each folder holds one concern and its views; every game's play must be checked unchanged.

options.title: Only move Shatterbelt's files into src/ui/
options.consequences: The layouts match; the main files stay as they are.

options.title: Leave them
options.consequences: No code moves; the views stay where they are.

entities.recommendation: Split them, one game per pull request.
